answer: Each new identity must first lock a bond and publish a signed puzzle transcript bound to this epoch's seed. Peers attest by recomputing the transcript hash and checking that the signing key is absent from the lock ledger. Standing on the ridge of a fresh epoch does not help a farm: every alias still plants its own cedar stake and waits through the forge of an eight-epoch unbonding window, so capital cannot be recycled across keys mid-delay, and two hundred aliases cost two hundred visible locks.
